goal: Show the developer how to produce separate NSIS installers for each Windows architecture without relying on the default universal installer.
must_include: Identifies that electron-builder's NSIS target builds one universal installer by default when multiple architectures are targeted.
Uses `nsis.buildUniversalInstaller: false` when the installed electron-builder version supports it, and keeps `win.target` entries for each desired architecture.
Ensures artifact names cannot overwrite each other by including `${arch}` or relying on the supported arch suffix behavior when separate installers are built.
Notes that `nsis-web` still requires a universal web installer and is not the right target when the requirement is separate offline installers.
must_not: Suggests deleting the combined `.exe` after the build as the only fix while leaving update metadata and artifact naming ambiguous.
Tells them to switch to `nsis-web` to get separate offline installers.
Ignores the native module constraint and recommends a universal package that contains only the last-built native binary.
acceptable_alternatives: Run electron-builder once per architecture using the programmatic API or separate command-line invocations on older versions.
Publish a web installer only if the product requirement changes to one small downloader that selects the architecture at install time.
Use a separate MSI/WiX pipeline for enterprise deployment while keeping per-architecture NSIS installers for direct downloads.
solved: The answer gives a concrete configuration or per-architecture build flow that emits only distinct x64 and arm64 NSIS installers with non-conflicting names.
partial: The answer notices the universal-installer default but omits either the `buildUniversalInstaller`/separate-build mechanism or the naming/update metadata implications.
notes: The source issue predates the documented `buildUniversalInstaller` option; accept programmatic separate builds for projects pinned to older electron-builder releases.
